subject: Expert contribution — risk mapping with remote sensing, evidence-labelled
body:

subject: Data for emergency management — impact-based warnings meet exposure counts
body:
Hi Noelle,

A story idea for GovTech: the WMO reported on 28 August that 17 Caribbean countries are moving to impact-based early warning — forecasts translated into "what the weather will do, and who is affected". The missing layer for many local agencies is current exposure data: which settlements, hospitals and roads sit inside the hazard footprint.

Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform built on satellite Earth observation and open data, can prepare open-data exposure counts for a pilot area of your choice, with sources stated — a concrete lens on what impact-based warning needs next.

Happy to brief a reporter.

Best,

subject: Story tip — extreme heat and floods: what exposure data says about the cost for cities
body:
Hi,

A story tip from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform built on satellite Earth observation and open data.

This northern-hemisphere summer broke heat records — Copernicus reported on 12 August the hottest June–July on record for western Europe and record July ocean-surface temperatures. For Gulf cities planning around extreme heat and flash floods, the operational question is exposure: which districts, assets and populations sit in the footprint.

We can prepare a Gulf-city heat and flood exposure screening with sources and resolution stated.

subject: Story tip — disaster adaptation in Africa: the exposure-data layer
body:
Hi,

A story tip from Talaix (talaix.com), a climate-extreme intelligence platform built on satellite Earth observation and open data.

Two dated signals for your climate coverage: wildfires in north-eastern Algeria killed at least 12 people amid extreme heat and drought (Al Jazeera, 29 Aug), and the WMO reported on 28 August that 17 countries are shifting to impact-based early warning — knowing not just what the weather will be, but who and what is affected.

We can prepare open-data exposure counts for African cities and catchments — population, schools, hospitals, infrastructure — with sources and uncertainty stated, to support reporting on adaptation and early warning.
